rows.en: Maybe it really was just a dream after all.{p}

The gathering I went to because Hino, my senior in the newspaper club, asked me to.
The six who gathered there vanished one by one, each time a story was told.{p}

And when all six had vanished, the masked girl appeared.
She hinted that the six were dead, and then she too vanished from before my eyes.{p}

I was a person named {b} {a}.
And I was a first-year at this school.{p}

And I was a member of the newspaper club, and Hino was there too.
And so I confirmed that the world I was in now was reality.
But one thing was different.
Just one thing was different from the reality I knew.{p}

It was that the newspaper club's plan to do a feature on the seven wonders had never existed in the first place.
Naturally, when I brought it up, Hino tilted his head with a puzzled look.
Akemi Iwashita.
Nozomu Kazama.
Makoto Shindo.
Tomoharu Hosoda.
Shoji Arai.
Reiko Fukuzawa.
Hino didn't know a single one of their names.
I checked the school roster.
But there wasn't a single student by any of those names.
Thinking I might have missed them, I checked again and again.
But it was wasted effort.
They didn't exist.
They were never students who belonged at this school.{p}

...Then what was it that I saw?
What had that gathering been in the first place?
Had I been daydreaming?
A terribly realistic dream?{p}

No, that was no dream.
Those six were undeniably there, laughing, breathing.
Even now I remember them so clearly that I could tell each of them apart by their faces, their laughter, even their scent.
The seven of us, who met and shared one fleeting moment in such a short time.
They exist.
I'm certain of it, and yet I go on living the same old everyday life, unable to clear away the thing lodged in my chest.
...And today, that old school building is being torn down.
The first term had ended, and it was already summer vacation.
What should I do?
Should I go to the school?{p}And see the old school building being torn down?
Go to the school
Don't go to the school
I could hear the noise of the construction from quite far away.{p}

...They're already tearing down the old school building.
I ran.
Just as I reached the school, the old building was coming down with a roar.
It was almost as if it had been waiting for me to arrive.
I staggered toward the old building as if I were being lured.
"It's dangerous, move aside."{p}One of the construction workers urged me to keep my distance.
Say you're covering it for the newspaper club
Move away as you're told
Ignore the warning and go closer

"Um, I'm with the newspaper club.
And, well, I was told to cover the demolition of the old school building..."
"Nobody told me about that."
The worker looked troubled and folded both arms.
"...Well, fine. Just don't get in the way."
At that, I bowed.
I approached the flattened wreckage of the old school building.
Now that it had come to this, there was no trace left of the old building, frightening as it had been, yet full of character.
It was nothing but a heap of garbage.{p}

"Heeeeey! A body! There's a body here!☆"
A loud voice rang out not far away.
Maybe somewhere in my heart I had been expecting that.
Amid the stirring crowd, I held back my eagerness and headed for the spot where the voice had come from too.
"...This poor soul hasn't been dead long."
"Ain't this a student from this school?"
"One... two... three... there's six of 'em!"
Everyone surrounded the bodies, gazing at them with deeply sympathetic eyes.{p}

There were six bodies in school uniforms.
Four were male.
Two were female.
They lay buried in the ruins of the rubble, piled on top of one another.
Every one of the bodies was pristine.
Perhaps because they lay face down, their faces couldn't be seen.
But I knew who they were.
I didn't need to look at their faces; I knew very well whose bodies these were.{p}

"Call the police!"
Someone shouted.
Then another voice rose from farther off.
"There's bones over here! There's a whole lotta skeletons buried here!"
"What the hell kind of school is this..."
People's voices flew back and forth, half appalled, half astonished.
Just how many human lives had this old school building devoured until now?{p}

In any case, those six had really existed.
Inside the old school building, at least, they had existed.
Their identities would surely never be confirmed.
But they had definitely been there.
If I'm in the real world now, that is...
The weight in my chest finally lifted, so I decided to head home.{p}

In the old school building, left unused for so long, residents of some unknowable world must have settled in.
And in that place they are born, they live, and they die.
Living inside the old school building, they must have known it would soon be destroyed.
And so, wanting to tell me something, they must have shown me those visions.
I must have had that strange experience because I was bewitched by the people who live in the old school building.{p}

...That was the thought that suddenly came to me.
Am I wrong to think so?
Or has my mind just gone strange, and I'm only seeing hallucinations?
Is the masked girl nothing but a figment of my own imagination?{p}
...The night had grown late.{p}What should I do?
Go to sleep now
Read a book
Maybe do some studying

I opened the drawer to take out something to write with.
In there was...{p}

That mask.
The mask lay carefully in the middle of the drawer, as if someone had placed it there.
The mask that had disappeared when I left the old school building.
It was here, in the drawer of the study desk in my own house.{p}What could it mean, that mask being here?
I'm being invited too
A gift from that girl
I'm still dreaming
Am I being invited?{p}

I picked up the mask.
The instant I did, I felt as though I had touched something I should never have touched.
What was it that had been in the old school building?
Where will the things that were in the old school building go now?{p}

Without realizing it, I held the mask up to my face.
The moment it touched, I felt dizzy for an instant, and my view changed completely.{p}

The scene I saw through the mask.
It was the old school building.
And standing in front of me was me.
This place is... isn't this the girls' restroom in the old school building?
To me in the mask, the me in front of me said just one thing.
"I don't want to see."{p}

...I see.
You don't want to see my face?
Then don't look.
At your own face.
I'm still in the nightmare.
In a pleasant nightmare.{p}

Forget it.
What good would it do to see something like that now?{p}

I flopped down on my bed.
It's always like this lately.
Did something inside me vanish along with those six?
I can't bring myself to do anything.
I let out a deep sigh.
...Heh.{p}
What?
I definitely heard something just now.{p}

I looked around the room.
Is someone there★
All I could see was my room, the same as always.
But that presence just now...
Heh heh...{p}

There it is again!
There really is someone in this room besides me.{p}

"Wh... Who's there?"
My voice cracked.
Whoever it was, their laughter grew louder.
And it was a voice I knew.
"How cold of you. Have you forgotten me already?"{p}

"Oh, but you can hear it, see?"
Just then, the owner of the mischievous voice appeared.
Suddenly, as if pulling open an invisible curtain.
I stared at her, unable to believe it.{p}

"Fu... kuzawa..."
The one standing before me was Reiko Fukuzawa.
"What's with that face? Like you've seen a ghost or something."
Even if she says that...
She vanished right in front of me.
She wasn't even on the roster.
Even just now, she appeared out of nowhere.
If she's not a ghost, then what exactly does she mean to say she is?{p}

"Shindo★"
At some point, Shindo had sat himself down on my desk.{p}

"You think nothing can exist in this world except what you can understand, don't you?"
In the chair beside him sat Hosoda.{p}
"Oh my, but I don't dislike that side of you."{p}
"Yes, it just goes to show how earnest you are, {a}."{p}

Iwashita, Arai, and even Kazama.
"N... No way..."
I rubbed my eyes without thinking.
Kazama shrugged.
"Hey now, you're not going to call a dashing, ultra-handsome heartthrob like me a hallucination, are you?"
The way he said it took away any urge to talk back.
No doubt about it, this was Kazama.{p}
Then... the others too?{p}

"Looks like you finally get it. It was us who told you about the seven wonders the other day."
Fukuzawa smiled sweetly.
"H-How..."
I murmured without thinking.{p}

But I wasn't really sure myself what I was asking.
There were so many things I wanted to ask.{p}
